name: s5_what_failed_in_18
title: Exp 18: the NLA does not state what the model uses
caption: Exp 18's ten synthetic rows: x = how strongly pushing the state moves the model's next-token odds (|z| vs 20 isotropic nulls; grey strip = rows with no next-token set), y = share of the NLA's 320 free readouts (40 items x 8) a judge marked as stating the property, with item-clustered bootstrap 95% intervals. The pre-registered rule 'states exactly when used' (it predicts stated right of the |z| = 3 line) got 5 of 10: LaTeX math is the most used row and is never stated, natural language has no next-token use and is stated 95%. 'Used' is the language here; the NLA's statements followed the statement shift instead (exp 28 later showed that only separates language from structure).
